newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU Parliament condemns army-rebel conflict.
newsitem.headline: EU Parliament condemns army-rebel conflict.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday condemned the fighting between the Zairean army and Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels, which has provoked an exodus of Rwandan and Burundi refugees from eastern Zaire.

"The European Parliament condemns the fighting between the Zairean army and the Banyamulenge armed bands and calls for an immediate cessation of hostilites," the European Union's directly elected assembly said in a resolution.
The Zairean government had a duty to protect the mainly Hutu refugees on its territory, some 250,000 of whom have fled the conflict in Uvira, the resolution continued.
Zaire complained to the United Nations on Thursday, accusing neighbouring Burundi and Rwanda, whose armies are dominated by Tutsis, of helping the Banyamulenge Tutsis.
The Banyamulenge came to Zaire from Rwanda 200 years ago and are locked in conflict over nationality with native Zaireans.

The EU parliament warned that the Great Lakes region was on the brink of all-out war and appealed to the countries in Central Africa to start talks aimed at achieving peace throughout the region and tackling the refugee crisis.
Euro-MPs also urged the European Commission to work with countries in the region to create corridors for supplying humanitarian aid to refugees fleeing Uvira camps.

Ethnic rivalries in eastern Zaire were heightened by the influx in mid-1994 of more than a million Hutu refugees from the civil war and massacres in Rwanda, in which up to a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus were killed.
